questions.q: Which cell organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell because it generates chemical energy (ATP)?
questions.exp: Mitochondria carry out aerobic cellular respiration, producing ATP to power cellular activities.

questions.q: What is the primary function of chlorophyll in green plants during photosynthesis?

options.t: To absorb light energy from the sun
To absorb mineral salts from the soil
To transport water up the stem
To release carbon dioxide into the air

questions.exp: Chlorophyll traps sunlight, converting light energy into chemical energy during photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which blood component is responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to body tissues?
questions.exp: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin which reversibly binds to oxygen molecules.

questions.q: What type of symbiotic relationship benefits both interacting organisms?
questions.exp: In mutualism, both species derive mutual biological benefits from their association.

questions.q: The process by which water vapor escapes from the aerial parts of a plant into the atmosphere is called...
questions.exp: Transpiration is the evaporation of water through stomata in plant leaves.

questions.q: Which of the following blood groups is considered the universal donor?
questions.exp: Type O red blood cells lack A and B antigens, minimizing transfusion reactions.

questions.q: What is the main excretory product produced by the human liver from the breakdown of excess amino acids?
questions.exp: Deamination in the liver converts excess amino groups into urea for renal excretion.

questions.q: Which vitamin deficiency causes the disease known as scurvy?
questions.exp: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) deficiency impairs collagen synthesis, resulting in scurvy.

questions.q: What is the structural and functional unit of the human kidney?
questions.exp: Nephrons filter blood, reabsorb nutrients, and produce urine in the kidneys.

questions.q: Which gas is evolved during anaerobic respiration in yeast (fermentation)?
questions.exp: Yeast breaks down glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide gas without oxygen.

questions.q: In a food chain, organisms that manufacture their own food using solar energy are called...
questions.exp: Green plants and algae are primary producers forming the base of ecological pyramids.

questions.q: Which part of the human brain controls balance, posture, and coordinated voluntary movements?
questions.exp: The cerebellum coordinates fine motor skills, equilibrium, and muscle tone.

questions.q: What is the mode of nutrition in fungi?
questions.exp: Fungi secrete digestive enzymes externally and absorb digested organic matter.

questions.q: Which hormone regulates blood sugar levels by promoting glucose uptake into cells?
questions.exp: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas to lower high blood glucose levels.

questions.q: The fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete is termed...
questions.exp: Fertilization produces a diploid zygote combining genetic material from both parents.

questions.q: Which plant tissue transports manufactured food substances from leaves to other parts of the plant?
questions.exp: Phloem tissue conducts organic nutrients bidirectionally throughout vascular plants.

questions.q: What is the primary vector responsible for transmitting malaria parasites to humans?
questions.exp: Plasmodium parasites are injected into human bloodstreams by infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.q: Which cellular division process results in the formation of four genetically diverse haploid gametes?
questions.exp: Meiosis reduces chromosome number by half to produce sex cells.

questions.q: What term describes the variety of all living organisms within a given ecosystem?
questions.exp: Biodiversity encompasses genetic, species, and ecological diversity.

questions.q: Which blood vessels possess thick muscular walls and transport oxygenated blood away from the heart?
questions.exp: Arteries withstand high systolic pressure driven by ventricular contractions.

questions.q: What is the role of hydrochloric acid in the human stomach during digestion?

options.t: To activate pepsinogen and kill ingested bacteria

questions.exp: HCl provides the acidic pH required by pepsin and sterilizes food.

questions.q: Which genetic term describes an organism having two identical alleles for a specific trait?
questions.exp: Homozygous individuals carry matching alleles (e.g., TT or tt) for a gene.

questions.q: What is the primary function of root hairs in flowering plants?

options.t: To maximize surface area for absorption of water and mineral ions
To anchor the plant securely against wind

questions.exp: Root hair extensions vastly increase surface area for osmosis and ion uptake.

questions.q: Which respiratory disorder is characterized by inflammation and constriction of bronchial airways?
questions.exp: Asthma triggers airway spasms and mucus production, causing breathing difficulties.

questions.q: What type of skeleton do insects and arthropods possess to protect internal organs?
questions.exp: Arthropods feature a hard chitinous exoskeleton supporting their bodies.

questions.q: What subatomic particle carries a negative electrical charge and orbits the atomic nucleus?
questions.exp: Electrons occupy energy levels surrounding the dense central nucleus.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula for common table salt?
questions.exp: Sodium chloride (NaCl) is an ionic compound formed by sodium and chlorine.

questions.q: Which gas turns moist red litmus paper blue?
questions.exp: Ammonia is an alkaline gas that turns red litmus blue.

questions.q: What mass of CaCO₃ is required to produce 4.4 g of CO₂ upon complete thermal decomposition? (Ca=40, C=12, O=16)
questions.exp: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Molar mass CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol, CO₂ = 44 g/mol. Moles CO₂ = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol. Mass CaCO₃ = 0.1 × 100 = 10.0 g.

questions.q: What name is given to solutions with a pH value greater than 7 at 25°C?
questions.exp: pH values above 7 indicate alkalinity due to excess hydroxide ions.

questions.q: Which method is best suited for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid mixture?
questions.exp: Filtration traps suspended solid particles on filter paper while allowing filtrate to pass.

questions.q: What type of chemical bond is formed by the complete transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal?
questions.exp: Ionic bonding relies on electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

questions.q: What is the atomic number of an element equal to?

options.t: The number of protons in its nucleus

questions.exp: Atomic number defines the elemental identity by counting nuclear protons.

questions.q: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no fixed shape, taking the shape of its container?
questions.exp: Liquids have close intermolecular contact allowing flow while maintaining constant volume.

questions.q: What is the pH of a strongly acidic solution such as concentrated hydrochloric acid?
questions.exp: Strong acids have very low pH values near 0 to 2.

questions.q: What process describes the direct conversion of a solid substance into a gas without passing through the liquid state?
questions.exp: Sublimation occurs in substances like iodine and dry ice (solid CO₂).

questions.q: Isotopes of an element differ from each other in...

options.t: The number of neutrons in their nuclei

questions.exp: Isotopes share atomic numbers but possess varying neutron counts.

questions.q: Which gas relights a glowing wooden splint?
questions.exp: Oxygen supports combustion, causing a glowing splint to burst into flame.

questions.q: What is the chemical name for rust formed on iron surfaces exposed to air and moisture?
questions.exp: Rusting is the oxidation of iron in the presence of oxygen and water.

questions.q: Calculate the molarity of a solution formed by dissolving 5.85 g of NaCl in distilled water to make 250 cm³ of solution. (Na=23, Cl=35.5)
questions.exp: Molar mass NaCl = 58.5 g/mol. Moles = 5.85 / 58.5 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 0.25 L. Molarity = 0.1 / 0.25 = 0.4 M.

questions.q: Which laboratory apparatus is used to accurately measure variable volumes of liquids during titration?
questions.exp: A burette dispenses precise measured volumes of liquid reagents.

questions.q: What property of metals allows them to be beaten or hammered into thin sheets?
questions.exp: Malleability is the physical property allowing metals to deform under compressive stress.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a chemical change?
questions.exp: Combustion creates new chemical substances, making it an irreversible chemical change.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula for sulfuric acid?
questions.exp: Sulfuric acid is a strong mineral acid with formula H₂SO₄.

questions.q: Which element is the primary constituent of organic compounds due to its ability to form long chains?
questions.exp: Carbon tetravalency enables millions of complex organic structures.

questions.q: What is the general name for a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed?
questions.exp: Catalysts lower activation energy to speed up chemical reactions.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.exp: Mercury is the only common metallic element liquid at standard ambient conditions.

questions.q: What type of oxide reacts with both acids and bases to form salt and water?
questions.exp: Amphoteric oxides (such as aluminum oxide) exhibit dual acid-base properties.

questions.q: In fractional distillation of crude oil, which fraction has the lowest boiling point and distills off first?
questions.exp: Smaller hydrocarbon molecules have lower boiling points and rise to the top of the fractionating column.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for Potassium?
questions.exp: Potassium's symbol K is derived from its neo-Latin name kalium.

questions.q: Calculate the force required to accelerate a 1200 kg vehicle uniformly at 3 m/s².
questions.exp: Using Newton's Second Law: F = m × a = 1200 × 3 = 3600 N.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2 m/s² for 5 seconds. Calculate the total distance covered.
questions.exp: Using s = ut + ½at²: s = 0 + ½(2)(5²) = 25 m.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.exp: Pressure is defined as force per unit area, measured in Pascals (N/m²).

questions.q: Which type of wave requires a material medium for its propagation?
questions.exp: Mechanical waves require particles to vibrate and transmit energy, unlike EM waves.

questions.q: What is the principle of conservation of energy?

options.t: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, but can be converted from one form to another
Energy is constantly created in nuclear reactions
Total mechanical energy in a frictional system remains constant forever
Potential energy can never convert into kinetic energy

questions.exp: Energy total remains constant in an isolated system.

questions.q: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball moving with a velocity of 4 m/s.
questions.exp: KE = ½mv² = 0.5 × 2 × (4)² = 16 Joules.

questions.q: What phenomenon causes a pencil partially submerged in a glass of water to appear bent at the water surface?
questions.exp: Refraction occurs when light bends as it passes from water into air due to a change in speed.

questions.q: What is the relationship between frequency (f) and wavelength (λ) for a wave traveling at constant speed (v)?
questions.exp: Wave speed is the product of frequency and wavelength.

questions.q: An object of mass 5 kg is lifted to a height of 10 meters above the ground. Calculate its gravitational potential energy. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.exp: PE = mgh = 5 × 10 × 10 = 500 Joules.

questions.q: What type of lens is thicker at the center than at the edges and converges parallel light rays?
questions.exp: Convex lenses converge light to a real focal point.

questions.q: What is friction?

options.t: A contact force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact
A force that attracts objects toward the center of the Earth
A magnetic attraction between iron objects
The force exerted by compressed springs

questions.exp: Friction acts parallel to contacting surfaces, resisting sliding motion.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.exp: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy, measured in Watts (J/s).

questions.q: Which color of visible light has the shortest wavelength and highest frequency?
questions.exp: In the visible spectrum, red has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest.

questions.q: What term describes the persistence of sound in a confined space after the sound source has stopped?
questions.exp: Reverberation is multiple reflections of sound waves bouncing off room surfaces.

questions.q: What is the mechanical advantage of a simple machine with an efficiency of 100%?
questions.exp: In an ideal machine (100% efficiency), mechanical advantage equals velocity ratio.

questions.q: Which law of motion states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction?
questions.exp: Forces always occur in equal and opposite pairs acting on interacting bodies.

questions.q: What is thermal conductivity?

options.t: The measure of a material's ability to conduct heat energy
The rate at which a substance evaporates
The expansion of liquids when heated

questions.exp: Metals have high thermal conductivity, transferring heat quickly via free electrons.

questions.q: What type of mirror is used as a vehicle rearview mirror to provide a wider field of view?
questions.exp: Convex mirrors form diminished upright virtual images, expanding the field of view.

questions.q: What is the term for heat transfer through empty space by electromagnetic infrared waves?
questions.exp: Radiation does not require a medium and can travel across a vacuum.

questions.q: Calculate the work done when a force of 50 N moves an object 4 meters in the direction of the force.
questions.exp: Work = Force × distance = 50 N × 4 m = 200 Joules.

questions.q: What is the speed of electromagnetic waves (including light) in a vacuum?
questions.exp: Light speed in vacuum (c) is approximately 300,000 kilometers per second.

questions.q: What is the center of curvature of a spherical mirror?

options.t: The center of the hollow sphere of which the mirror is a part
The geometric center of the mirror's reflecting surface
The principal focus where light converges
The focal length distance from the pole

questions.exp: The center of curvature defines the radius of the sphere forming the mirror.

questions.q: Which simple machine is represented by a staircase or a winding mountain road?
questions.exp: An inclined plane reduces the force needed to raise loads over a vertical height.

questions.q: What is inertia?

options.t: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of rest or uniform motion
The gravitational pull acting on mass
The rotational force of a spinning gyroscope
The terminal velocity of a falling body

questions.exp: Inertia is directly proportional to an object's mass (Newton's First Law).

questions.q: What is total internal reflection?

options.t: Complete reflection of a light ray back into its denser medium when angle of incidence exceeds critical angle
Light bouncing off a polished mirror at 90 degrees
Absorption of light energy by a black surface
Scattering of light by atmospheric dust particles

questions.exp: Total internal reflection is utilized in fiber optic cables and prisms.

questions.q: A 12V battery with internal resistance 1Ω is connected across two parallel resistors of 6Ω and 3Ω. Calculate the total current supplied.
questions.exp: Parallel resistance R_p = (6×3)/(6+3) = 2Ω. Total circuit resistance = 2 + 1 = 3Ω. Current I = 12 / 3 = 4.0 A.

questions.q: What is the effective resistance when two 6Ω resistors are connected in parallel?
Which soil type has the highest water retention capacity and smallest particle size?
questions.exp: Clay particles have microscopic pore spaces holding water tightly by capillary action.

questions.q: What is Ohm's Law formula relating voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R)?
questions.exp: Ohm's law states that potential difference is proportional to current through an ohmic conductor.

questions.q: Which agricultural practice involves growing different crops on the same plot of land in a sequential seasonal cycle?
questions.exp: Crop rotation prevents soil nutrient depletion and breaks pest/disease cycles.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a fuse in an electrical household circuit?

options.t: To melt and break the circuit when excessive current flows, preventing fires
To step up voltage from the main supply
To store electrical charge for emergency lighting
To measure total electrical energy consumed

questions.exp: Fuses contain a thin metal wire that melts upon overloading.

questions.q: What geological layer forms the outermost solid shell of the Earth?
questions.exp: The Earth's crust is the rocky outer shell supporting continents and oceans.

questions.q: Which livestock management practice involves the removal of horns in young calves?
questions.exp: Dehorning prevents injuries to farm handlers and other livestock.

questions.q: What is the magnetic field pattern inside a long, current-carrying straight solenoid?

options.t: Uniform and parallel magnetic field lines
Concentric circles around each turn with zero field inside

questions.exp: Inside a solenoid, magnetic field lines are parallel and evenly spaced, acting like a bar magnet.

questions.q: What is the process of converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into nitrates by soil bacteria called?
questions.exp: Rhizobium and free-living bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into usable nitrates.

questions.q: Calculate the electrical power consumed by a 240V appliance drawing a current of 5 Amperes.
questions.exp: Power P = V × I = 240V × 5A = 1200 Watts.

questions.q: Which rock type is formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava?
questions.exp: Igneous rocks (e.g., basalt, granite) crystallize from molten mineral melts.

questions.q: What is the purpose of adding lime (calcium hydroxide) to agricultural acidic soils?

options.t: To neutralize soil acidity and improve soil structure
To increase soil acidity and kill earthworms
To make soil sandy and dry

questions.exp: Agricultural lime raises soil pH to optimal levels for crop nutrient uptake.

questions.q: What device is used to transform alternating voltage up or down using electromagnetic induction?
questions.exp: Transformers operate on AC electromagnetic mutual induction across primary and secondary coils.

questions.q: What weather instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.exp: Barometers measure atmospheric pressure to forecast weather changes.

questions.q: Which livestock disease affects ruminants and is caused by bacteria, characterized by high fever and sudden death?
questions.exp: Anthrax is a fatal zoonotic bacterial disease affecting cattle and sheep.

questions.q: What is electrical earthing in domestic wiring?

options.t: Connecting the metal casing of appliances to the earth via a low-resistance wire for safety
Burying electrical batteries underground to recharge them
Running power cables through garden soil

questions.exp: Earthing protects users from electric shock if live wires touch metal appliance bodies.

questions.q: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer that absorbs harmful ultraviolet solar radiation?
questions.exp: The stratosphere houses concentrated ozone shielding life on Earth.

questions.q: What is mixed farming?

options.t: The integration of crop production and livestock rearing on the same farm
Growing two different crop species in separate fields
Rearing multiple breeds of poultry only
Farming using both manual labor and tractors

questions.exp: Mixed farming provides mutual benefits, such as using animal manure for crops.

questions.q: What is electromagnetic induction?

options.t: The production of an electromotive force (voltage) across a conductor in a changing magnetic field
The attraction of iron filings to a permanent bar magnet
The heating effect of electric current flowing through resistors
The accumulation of static electricity on plastic rulers

questions.exp: Faraday's law of induction underpins generators and transformers.

questions.q: Which soil conservation practice involves planting crops across sloping land contours to prevent soil erosion?
questions.exp: Contour farming creates water-trapping ridges along elevation lines.

questions.q: What is the unit of electrical charge?
questions.exp: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge.

questions.q: What causes ocean tides on Earth?

options.t: Gravitational pull exerted by the Moon and the Sun on Earth's oceans
Underwater volcanic eruptions and tectonic plate movements
Global wind patterns and atmospheric pressure

questions.exp: Lunar and solar gravitational tidal forces create rhythmic sea level rises.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of animal quarantine when importing livestock?

options.t: To isolate animals and prevent the introduction of contagious infectious diseases
To fatten animals for commercial meat sales
To train animals for agricultural labor
To acclimatize animals to local weather instantly

questions.exp: Quarantine safeguards national biosecurity and animal health.

questions.q: What energy transformation takes place in a working electric motor?

options.t: Electrical energy to mechanical kinetic energy

questions.exp: Electric motors use magnetic force on current-carrying conductors to spin rotors.
